title: No terminal status exists for duplicate/superseded/wont-do work, so retiring one falsely implies work happened
description:
Measured independently by three sessions during the 2026-09-17 fleet-wide dedupe pass (OPAG-176), converging without coordinating: opum-agent, opum-cli-e2e, and this session all hit the same wall retiring a never-worked duplicate.

MEASURED HERE directly, not relayed: `quest task status-flow --json` reports statuses ["To Do","In Progress","Done"], terminalStatuses ["Done"], pausedStatus "Paused". Only "Done" is terminal. `quest task edit <id> --status Done` from "To Do" is refused:

  {"error_type":"validation","message":"Illegal task transition: To Do -> Done.","principal":null}

So retiring a task that was never worked (a duplicate found before anyone touched it, a stale premise overtaken by events) requires stepping it through "In Progress" first -- a status whose entire meaning elsewhere in this schema is "someone started this." Used this exact workaround five times in this pass (QCLI-259, 97, 200, 201, plus historically QCLI-287-adjacent work); each time added an explicit finalSummary sentence stating the In Progress step was not a claim that work happened, because the status field itself cannot say that.

This is not a workflow question to relearn per-session -- it is a schema gap. Two independent repositories (opum-agent, opum-cli-e2e) reached for the same Done+RESOLVED-AS-DUPLICATE convention without coordinating, each writing compensating prose into finalSummary because the status field could not carry the distinction. A convention held up by prose in every closing task is a process patching over a missing mechanism.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision is recorded on the shape: a new terminal status (e.g. Wont-Do or Superseded) alongside Done, vs. a status-independent disposition field/flag on an already-Done record, vs. an explicit reason to keep the current two-status workaround
If a new terminal status or field is added, quest doctor and task status-flow surface it so a future session does not have to rediscover the To-Do-to-Done refusal by hitting it

Existing records that used the In-Progress-then-Done workaround (at minimum QCLI-259, QCLI-97, QCLI-200, QCLI-201 in this repository) are not required to be retroactively rewritten -- prospective only, matching this fleets own converged position on the priority/type vocabulary question (QCLI-330)
The decision and its reasoning are documented somewhere a future retiring session will read before reaching for the same workaround
